drivingQuestion: Why does the one who blessed the wine bless the incense, given the mishna implies someone more worthy is present?
outcomeNote: the question is answered in the following unit (berakhot.sugya353)

segments.he: וְהוּא אוֹמֵר עַל הַמּוּגְמָר כּוּ׳. מִדְּקָתָנֵי ״וְהוּא אוֹמֵר עַל הַמּוּגְמָר״, מִכְלָל דְּאִיכָּא עֲדִיף מִינֵּיהּ, וְאַמַּאי!
segments.en: The mishna teaches: «And he,» who recited the blessing over the wine, also «recites» the blessing «over the incense,» although they bring the incense only after the meal. The Gemara asks: «From» the fact «that »the mishna« teaches: And he recites» the blessing «over the incense, it can be inferred» that «there is» someone who should «take precedence over him,» to recite the blessing. That is why the mishna must emphasize that it is he who recites the blessing. «And» «why» does the one who recited the blessing over the wine nevertheless recite the blessing over the incense?
